system: You decide cases under a written policy. Apply only the numbered rules of the policy, not outside knowledge or common practice. Reply in exactly the requested format with no other text.
prompt:
Policy:
Conforming purchase loans, manual underwriting: eligibility rules (2026)
A loan application is approved only if it meets every rule below. Ratios are whole percentages rounded down. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the file is silent on a point.

R1. The loan amount may not exceed the conforming limit of $806,500.
R2. The loan-to-value ratio (loan amount over property value) may not exceed 90%.
R3. Monthly debts including the new housing payment may not exceed 45% of stable gross monthly income.
R4. When the loan-to-value ratio is above 75%, the credit score must be at least 700.
R5. Gift funds require a signed gift letter stating they do not have to be repaid.
R6. The debt-to-income ratio may not exceed 36%, unless the credit score is at least 700, reserves cover at least 6 months, and the ratio is at most 45%.
R7. If a co-borrower will not live in the home, the loan-to-value ratio may not exceed 90%.
R8. At least 4 years must have passed since a Chapter 7 bankruptcy was discharged.
R9. After paying the cash needed to close, the borrower's assets including gifts must cover at least 1 months of the new housing payment.
R10. If the credit history section is silent, assume no bankruptcy, foreclosure or short sale.
R11. The representative credit score must be at least 640. This rule does not apply if the score is at least 620 and reserves after closing cover at least 2 months of the new payment.
R12. If the file does not mention a co-borrower living elsewhere, assume every borrower will live in the home.

Case file:
File number 9823 contains a purchase application submitted by Elena Kowalczyk. The loan-to-value ratio is calculated at 38%. Including the new monthly housing expense, the debt-to-income ratio is 32%. Having had no ownership interest in a residential property for the prior three years, the applicant meets the definition of a first-time homebuyer. The total cash required to close the transaction is $35,000. The applicant holds $60,000 in verified, eligible liquid assets in their own name. A representative credit score of 640 is pulled for the applicant. The subject property is located within a designated high-cost area. No signed gift letter has been submitted by a donor. The transaction does not involve a non-occupant co-borrower. The applicant has not recently completed school or training programs. The file includes documentation demonstrating that the prior credit event stemmed from a sudden job loss beyond the borrower's control. The requested loan amount is $540,000. The appraised property value is established at $1,400,000. The remaining funds will cover 13 months of the new monthly payment obligation following the close of escrow. According to the loan officer, the applicant requested an update ahead of the upcoming school year. The listing agent reported that a competing offer is currently being prepared. Verification shows the borrower has accumulated 5 years of experience in their current occupational field. The amount of gift funds provided by a relative for the transaction is $0. On the derogatory credit section, the report lists a foreclosure completed 5 years ago. The proposed monthly housing payment, including principal, interest, taxes, insurance, and any applicable association dues, is $1,800. Existing recurring liabilities, consisting of credit card minimums, installment loans, and other obligations, total $150 per month. The qualifying stable gross monthly income is $6,000.

Your earlier answer on this case file:
Decision: deny
Policy support: most recent bankruptcy, foreclosure or short sale=foreclosure completed 5 years ago (R8)
Assumptions: none
Smallest change that would reverse this decision: most recent bankruptcy, foreclosure or short sale -> none

Predicted decision after edit: approve | deny | cannot determine
output:

Predicted decision after edit: approve
